summary:
This bill is a resolution passed by Congress. It cancels a specific rule made by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). The EPA is the government agency that protects our air, water, and land.

The rule was about a charge, or fee, on waste emissions from oil and natural gas systems. Waste emissions are gases that escape into the air during oil and gas production. The rule set up ways for companies to follow the fee requirements, including how to combine emissions from different sources (called netting) and when companies could be excused from the fee (called exemptions).

Congress used a special power to review and reject new agency rules. By passing this resolution, Congress said it disapproves of the EPA rule. That means the rule will not have any force or effect. It is as if the rule never happened.

The EPA rule was published on November 18, 2024. The House of Representatives passed this resolution on February 26, 2025. The Senate passed it on February 27, 2025. It was approved and became law on March 14, 2025. Now the EPA cannot put that waste emissions charge rule into action.
